subgroup_label: ischemic optic neuropathy/NAION benchmark (secondary outcome; 2004Q1-2026Q1, CASEID-latest dedup, primary suspect)
evidence_quote: The semaglutide ischemic optic neuropathy/NAION benchmark comprised 650 reports... median age was ... 60 years for the ischemic benchmark (430/650 known).
notes: Primary endpoint of paper is optic neuritis (crude ROR 11.67, 60 vs 15 events vs SGLT2i/metformin), NOT NAION; no ROR reported for ION benchmark in main text (Supplementary Table 16). n_reports_other_total = pooled SGLT2i/metformin comparator reports. 645/650 ION reports in 2024-2026; 358 HP vs 232 consumer/legal reporters; 8/60 optic neuritis reports co-coded an ION term. Research prototype; not for clinical use.

evidence_quote: We also identified ophthalmologic adverse events, including optic ischemic neuropathy (ROR = 4.42, 95% CI = 1.41-13.87; N = 144).
notes: Active comparator = liraglutide (T2D indication). 'N = 144' as printed; unclear whether it is semaglutide-only case count or total. Outcome is MedDRA PT 'optic ischemic neuropathy' (includes AION/NAION, cannot distinguish). Report totals are after indication + SOC filtering (13,168 sema T2D; 1,201 lira T2D). Signal required ROR LL>1, N>=3 plus one other positive metric (PRR/IC/EBGM values only in figure).

evidence_quote: Additional AEs included suicidal ideation (ROR = 6.28...) and optic ischemic neuropathy (ROR = 11.46, 95% CI = 6.21-21.16; N = 147).
notes: Pooled sensitivity analysis vs non-GLP-1RA comparators (metformin n=12,206 T2D reports; orlistat n=53 obesity reports). Overlaps with semaglutide-vs-liraglutide row (same reports).

evidence_quote: Semaglutide demonstrated a strong post-marketing safety signal for optic ischaemic neuropathy (355 reports; ROR 94.45, 95% CI: 83.02-107.45; PRR 93.77, 95% CI: 82.48-106.61).
notes: PRR 95% CI 82.48-106.61. Mean (not median) age 59 y; disability 18%, hospitalization 11%. Outcome MedDRA PT 'optic ischaemic neuropathy'. Background = whole FAERS. Near-identical semaglutide ROR (94.534) reported by FAERS component of PMID 42768849 (different authors) - likely same OpenVigil extraction; avoid double counting.

evidence_quote: Tirzepatide and liraglutide also exhibited significant safety signals (49 reports; ROR 2.94, 95% CI: 2.20-3.93; PRR 2.94...

notes: Liraglutide FAERS ROR 4.519 (2.617-7.802) in PMID 42768849 likely same extraction.

notes: Outcome = ischaemic optic neuropathy (ION). Multivariable AOR Wegovy vs Ozempic = 4.74 (CI not in abstract). 31,774 = total semaglutide cases analysed. Paywalled; CIs not available.

evidence_quote: Of 73,636 global Individual Case Safety Reports (ICSRs) related to Semaglutide ... 91 were associated with the adverse reaction NAION.
notes: Descriptive only (no disproportionality metric in abstract). Denmark 38 (41.8%), Australia 9, France 7; 50/91 (54.9%) aged 45-74; 97.8% serious; 'significant' share male (pct not given). Overlaps VigiBase rows of PMID 41021211.

evidence_quote: Semaglutide exhibited the strongest signals, notably for NAION (ROR = 40.18, IC025 = 2.06 in VigiBase and ROR = 31.46, IC025 = 4.84 in FAERS), with 2,878 cases in VigiBase and 2,047 in FAERS.
notes: '2,878 cases in VigiBase' is ambiguous (likely all semaglutide ocular AE cases, not NAION cases; implausible vs 91 NAION ICSRs in PMID 41026313) - not entered as NAION count. Liraglutide/lixisenatide: no VigiBase signal. Early onset (<=30 d) common for semaglutide.

evidence_quote: ...NAION (ROR = 40.18, IC025 = 2.06 in VigiBase and ROR = 31.46, IC025 = 4.84 in FAERS), with 2,878 cases in VigiBase and 2,047 in FAERS.

evidence_quote: 96 NAION cases were retrieved (83 to semaglutide)... median time to onset of 186 days. An SDR emerged only for semaglutide (ROR=17.57; 95 %CI=13.93-21.90)
notes: Median TTO 186 d may refer to all 96 GLP-1RA NAION cases. SDR only for semaglutide among GLP-1RAs (13 non-semaglutide GLP-1RA cases, no SDR). Remained significant in active-comparator (incl. SGLT2i) and therapeutic-area restricted analyses (values not in abstract).

evidence_quote: Semaglutide showed a significant ROR and PRR for NAION, suggesting a stronger association compared to other GLP-1 receptor agonists.
